solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Place has last of paint stripper

parts.note: a locus is a place or position, especially in mathematics or law

indicators.note: the final letter of the word paint is the piece taken here

explanation.surface: A location stocks the dregs of some paint remover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint stripper' reads as one item, but 'stripper' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Locust swarms strip fields bare of crops, so the insect is a stripper of vegetation.

clue.text: Impertinence and criticism, cosmetic

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk or impertinence
stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in 'take stick'

explanation.surface: Cheek and censure are said to be merely superficial.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured stick applied to the mouth is a common cosmetic product.

clue.text: Double feature is toast

indicators.note: says the facial feature is written twice in a row

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A cinema double bill is raised in salute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double feature' looks like a cinema pairing, but it is a facial feature twice.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal drinking salutation said when raising glasses.

clue.text: Notice zit

definitions.meaning: to catch sight of or see

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to catch sight of; the other is a skin blemish or pimple.

clue.text: Private drinker, man stuck on booze in the end

indicators.note: the drinker and the man are attached after the letter from booze
the final letter of the word booze is the piece used

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A secretive drinker, a fellow hooked on alcohol in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck on' means the drinker and the man come after the letter from 'booze'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is confined to a select few, hence private rather than public.

clue.text: Unbreakable short tape for breaking

indicators.note: breaking the letters apart lets them be reassembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Something can't be broken, being too brief a ribbon for snapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass that resists smashing is described as able to withstand breakage.

clue.text: Course it's a pin!

definitions.meaning: a line of action or approach
a short nail with a broad head, a drawing pin

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a route is actually a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a line of approach, from sailing; the other is a small nail.

clue.text: Appreciate sweet pickle

definitions.meaning: a tangy condiment, such as a chutney

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a sugary preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to enjoy; the other is a chutney-like condiment.

clue.text: Cold milk brought over that attracts felines

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: the word for milk is turned over, so read upward in this down clue

parts.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk

explanation.surface: Chilled milk delivered that lures cats.
explanation.walkthrough: PINTA, from 'a pint of milk', is British slang made famous by an old advertising slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: This mint-family herb draws and excites domestic cats.

clue.text: Can no teacher start to play around?

indicators.note: signals that the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written
pupils address a male teacher as sir

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word play is the piece used

explanation.surface: A question of whether a teacher may refuse to start fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the whole run of three pieces back to front, not just the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for jail, a synonym for a place of confinement.

clue.text: Pop takes share as legendary adulterer

indicators.note: the first piece takes on the second, which follows it

parts.note: to lance a boil is to pop or pierce it
a lot is a portion or share

explanation.surface: Dad claims his portion, posing as a famous philanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a father, but it is the verb to pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend this knight conducted an affair with Queen Guinevere, wife of King Arthur.

clue.text: Christmas tree certainly not tidy — that's about right!

indicators.note: the phrase of refusal goes round the letter for right

parts.note: no way is an emphatic refusal
to spruce up is to make neat

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to tidy the festive tree, insisting that's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidy' looks like an instruction in the surface, but it supplies the second word of the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This European conifer is the species traditionally used for festive trees in Britain.

clue.text: Second sucker

definitions.meaning: a very short moment, as in 'just a jiffy'
a bloodsucking parasite that clings to animals

explanation.surface: A runner-up who is also a gullible fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a brief moment of time, and a blood-feeding arachnid parasite.

clue.text: Saw too much in a flash

indicators.note: the excessive piece goes inside the brief moment

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant or flash
OTT is short for over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: Someone glimpsed far too much in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but it is the noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, a synonym for a guiding phrase.

clue.text: Drink doubling sexual allure? On the contrary!

parts.note: doubling as means serving as, giving the word as

indicators.note: says the sex appeal word is turned the other way round

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A beverage that doubles your sex appeal, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Roof off huge private chamber, house in sub-zero temperatures

indicators.note: the top letter is removed, as in a down clue the first letter is the roof

parts.note: big means huge
a loo is British slang for a toilet, a private little room

explanation.surface: An enormous privy with no roof provides shelter in the freezing cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roof off' removes the B at the top of BIG LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome of snow blocks built by Inuit people is a dwelling in Arctic cold.

clue.text: A little English wine unlike claret

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'

explanation.surface: A small English wine that differs from Bordeaux red.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red, so a wine unlike it is the pale-coloured kind.

clue.text: Embarrassing characterisation initially worrying the cast

indicators.note: the first letter of the word characterisation is the piece used
to cast is to throw or mould, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An awkward portrayal at first unsettles the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors, but it is the anagram signal for WORRYING THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes you wince with discomfort is excruciatingly embarrassing.

clue.text: Fast pace finally comes in a bit — that's brilliant

indicators.note: the fasting season and the letter go inside the small amount

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: the last letter of the word pace is the piece used

explanation.surface: A rapid pace finally arrives briefly, which is great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed but is the Christian season of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: A gifted or highly skilled person can be called brilliant.

clue.text: Puzzle, don't be as tame?

definitions.meaning: an urging to be less tame, i.e. to be more untamed, read as two words

explanation.surface: A conundrum: advice not to be so docile.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to baffle; the other splits the word into an instruction to be more untamed.

clue.text: Synthetic material upon leathery cracks (or treating your elephant?)

indicators.note: to crack something breaks it apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man-made coating applied to cracked leather, as one might use on a wrinkly elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthetical question is a playful aside: an elephant's skin is leathery and cracked, and this material is a protective varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a plastic polymer used in foams, varnishes and coatings, made artificially.

clue.text: 59 seconds up for cloud?

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: fifty-nine seconds is less than a minute, sub plus min

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a minute short is a raised cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB (below) + MIN (minute) is a time under a minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a rain-bearing grey cloud, or a halo of light.

clue.text: Pacific island endlessly in conflict, one's spotted

indicators.note: the shortened island sits inside the word for clash

parts.note: to jar is to clash, and a jar is a conflict

indicators.note: the last letter of the island name is cut off

parts.note: Guam is a US island territory in the western Pacific

explanation.surface: A Pacific island perpetually at war, where someone has been sighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's spotted' reads as someone being seen, but it describes the animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: This big cat of the Americas has a coat marked with rosettes, so it is spotted.

clue.text: Country where I once was president?

parts.note: ran, as in ran the country, means was in charge

explanation.surface: Someone asks which nation they used to lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in the Middle East, formerly Persia.

clue.text: On which a thread coils around

indicators.note: the word for coils is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: loops are coils or twists

explanation.surface: Describes a reel with cotton wound round it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, so the wordplay and the definition overlap.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel or bobbin is the thing that thread is wound on.

clue.text: Monster returning, bite your nails!

indicators.note: the captured letters read from right to left
to nail is to catch and hold, so the words grip the letters within them

explanation.surface: A beast is coming back, so chew your fingernails in fright!
explanation.walkthrough: 'nails' looks like fingernails being bitten, but it signals the letters held in 'bite your', taken backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a legendary monster.

clue.text: In oral I'm pretty slack

indicators.note: the answer is found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being rather lax in a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floppy without firmness is slack.

clue.text: A game that's a match

definitions.meaning: a card game where players call out on matching cards
a pair that corresponds exactly, the call when two cards are alike

explanation.surface: A sport that is also a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a children's card game; the other is the cry when two items are identical.

clue.text: Loudly complain about wood in shop

indicators.note: says the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: boo means jeer or complain, and teak is a hardwood, so to boo teak is to complain about wood

explanation.surface: Someone noisily objects to the timber in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fashionable store selling clothes or gifts is a shop.

clue.text: Most central parts of Brunei, Mauritania and Sweden in agreement

indicators.note: the two letters at the very heart of each country name are taken

explanation.surface: Three nations' heartlands are said to be of one mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Each name has an even length, so its middle is two letters: UN, IT and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are united share one view, so they agree.

clue.text: Wanting to be beaten

definitions.meaning: short of money, as in '... for cash'

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is lacking funds; the other is punished with a leather band.

clue.text: Web designer beginning to poke inside back of computer

indicators.note: the letter from poke is placed within the word for back

parts.note: the back of something, such as a page, is one side of it

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word poke is used
taken with computer, the final letter is the piece wanted

explanation.surface: A website builder starts jabbing about inside the rear of a PC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Web designer' looks like a computer job, but it is the creature that spins a web; the computer surface feeds the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-legged creature spins silk webs, making it a designer of webs.
